The common-multiplier selection counts the actual relation on the actual lag set. Its proof is a genuine finite union/averaging argument. In the final theorem the existence premise is discharged by the actual induction hypothesis; it is not an unproved input at the root.

The dense-power inverse chooses both its output bound and actual length threshold before x,N. The true lower bound N^e>=N for e>0 enforces the original epsilon restriction. The genuine strong recurrence is applied to actual n*x samples. Dividing only by positive delta and N^e, it then clears the true denominator to get N^(e+1) control.

Actual lag h has N-h>=tau*N; the lower-degree bound on its true top coefficient transfers to N^(d+1) norm(h*q*(d+2)*alpha)<=C. The multiplier and degree factor are retained; arbitrary real coefficients and negative phases are allowed. The explicit small-N case uses Q=1 and the actual period-one half-period norm bound. Thus the top inverse covers ALL positive lengths, even though the analytic induction uses large lengths.

The counterexample is about an auxiliary unrestricted positive-lag density assertion, not the polynomial leading inverse, the quantitative Leibman theorem or the original prize target.
